Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Resident Evil Combat, one complete static creature sprite study with transparent background.
Input image 1 is the sole anatomy, edition, identity and materials reference; it is a documentary game render, not a generated pose to imitate. Create one independent LEFT-facing full-body pose, not a horizontal mirror or traced copy.
Subject and constraints: A single Adder snake from Resident Evil remake (2002). Its mouth is closed, its low broad head has the same pale cream facial stripes, and its continuous slender body has the brown-gold scale pattern shown. Pose the entire snake in a calm sinuous S-curve, with muzzle pointing decisively LEFT and tapered tail extending to the right. No legs, arms, added horns, cobra hood or forked body. The complete fine tail tip must remain visible.
Composition: one figure only, completely visible. Use generous transparent margins of about 10% beyond EVERY outermost point, including thin tips and equipment. Aim for a readable fighting-game side/three-quarter presentation, not a frontal portrait. Preserve source-specific handedness and asymmetries. Reconstruct only the change of pose needed; do not redesign the creature or invent new identifying features.
Style: match the attached game's realistic 3D rendering, original materials, colors and proportions, with readable neutral light and no added outline or rim glow. Preserve the edition's model detail level rather than adding photoreal microdetail.
Background: genuinely transparent alpha. No floor, cast/contact shadow, grey/brown matte, smoke, backdrop, vignette or opaque checkerboard. No labels, text, logos, UI, collage, duplicate body or animation grid. Keep body surfaces opaque and anti-aliased edges clean.
This is a generated adaptation for review, not a certified 1:1 original game frame.
